transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Start time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jared Lopez (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Atlas Lead Eng), Tom Reynolds (PM), Sara Kim (MLOps), Luis Ortega (Platform)
Link to deck / artifacts: https://redwood.example/pocs/atlas-weekly (deck), https://bits.example/benchmarks/atlas (benchmark sheet)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Reviewed last week's integration changes: SDK tool/function calling and structured-output schema enforcement.
- Customer ran smoke tests; saw some malformed JSON responses when model used streaming + function calls.
- Discussed retry/backoff, SDK validation, and result post-processing.
- Next: Redwood to provide updated SDK examples and Dedicated test cluster creds; Atlas to share sample events and run 10k-run; schedule Dedicated benchmarks.

Transcript:
00:00 Maya: hey everyone good to see you all, uh thanks for making time, quick check — can we do a quick round of who we are?
00:07 Priya: yeah priya here lead eng, i've been pairing with sara on the sdk bits and the function call wiring, thanks.
00:12 Tom: tom product, focusing on output format for the front-end UX — we need predictable fields.
00:18 Jared: jared from redwood se, i'll jump into the technical bits, latency, configs, and the dedicated test plan.
00:24 Sara: sara, m-l ops, mostly running the pipelines and the CI tests, saw a few flaky responses last run.
00:29 Luis: luis platform, i'll help with the dedicated env and creds, thanks.
00:35 Maya: cool, agenda: quick status, go over the malformed structured-output issue, SDK changes for tool/function calling, streaming behavior, then next steps.

01:02 Priya: from our side, we wired the sdk per the example but when we enabled streaming plus function-calls we got partial JSON sometimes, the front end chokes. example attached in the bug thread.
01:18 Sara: yep, we saw like 3-5% of responses where the JSON object is truncated at the end, looks like the closing brace is missing or there are escape issues.
01:26 Jared: ok that sounds like streaming cut while function payload still pending — a couple quick questions, are you using automatic schema validation in the SDK or custom post-parse?
01:36 Priya: currently custom post-parse, we added a tiny validator but it's forgiving, we wanted to avoid throwing in edge cases but it's breaking some downstream consumers.
01:45 Jared: got it; two angles: SDK-level liveness/stream reassembly to prefer complete JSON, and server-side config — we can enable "structured_output_enforce" in the model route which will return a canonical schema or an error if not match. that said enforcement can increase latency.
01:58 Tom: so is enforcement something we can toggle per-route? for dev vs prod?
02:05 Jared: yes per-route toggle, yes. dev you can be lenient, prod you can enforce. also we have preflight validation that can return a validation result in a lightweight header without full body for quick checks.
02:16 Priya: interesting, do you have recommended backoff + retry patterns for streaming case?
02:21 Jared: yes, we recommend a small client-side buffer for streaming chunks + an assemble timeout of ~500ms, then retry the call with same input and a 'resume' token when the server supported resume is available. our SDK exposes .resume() helper.
02:34 Sara: we tried a naive retry and that made duplicates in our event log, so we need idempotency keys too.
02:40 Jared: yep include idempotency keys; SDK supports auto-idempotency if you pass event_id. we can show snippet.

03:05 Maya: jared, can you walk through the SDK snippet you mentioned for function/tool calling and structured output enforcement?
03:10 Jared: sure, quick pseudo-code — (he's reading) "const client = Redwood.Client({apiKey}); const res = await client.generate({model: 'redwood-turbo-16k', input, tools: [inventoryTool], structuredOutput: {schema: productSchema, enforce: true}, stream: true});" — the key bits are tools array and structuredOutput with schema.
03:34 Priya: is the schema here a JSON Schema or do you support typed templates?
03:40 Jared: we accept JSON Schema v7-ish style, plus a simplified field mapping helper that maps model keys to your front-end keys. also we support a 'coerce' option that will try to coerce primitives (e.g., strings -> ints) but we don't recommend in strict prod.
03:55 Tom: what's the error shape when enforcement fails? we want to display a friendly error in UI.
04:00 Jared: the response will contain a validation object: {valid: false, errors: [...], suggestion: "call model with more context"} and an optional 'closest_attempt' string. again these are plumbed through headers if you prefer not to get full body.

04:32 Priya: ok on the malformed json, we still see issues after we applied the new assemble logic — one weird thing: sometimes the function call payload is emitted as plain text tokens and not wrapped in the function call wrapper in the transcript.
04:45 Jared: that could be a tokenization thing where the model decides to output raw text; to avoid this we recommend using either the SDK function-call hints (explicit function signatures) or a higher temperature lock for deterministic calls. temperature 0 to 0.2 for function calls is typical.
04:58 Sara: we run at temp 0.5 in prod for creative suggestions, but for strict structural responses we can run a separate route. would that be extra cost?
05:05 Jared: it depends — running two routes means two model invocations per event if you do both in sequence. alternative is to call a structured route first (cheap smaller context) and only call creative route on fallback. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching to reduce per-token cost.

06:10 Tom: can we talk about latency — our SLA needs 300ms p95 for the UI, is that realistic with structured enforcement?
06:18 Jared: 300ms p95 is tight for generation with structured enforcement and streaming. For short payloads and a small model (e.g., redwood-turbo-4k quantized on Dedicated), we can approach sub-300ms p95 with optimized kernels and prefix caching. But for larger contexts or chain of tool calls, expect 500-800ms. We should run an empirical benchmark on your 1k sample events.
06:40 Luis: i'll coordinate Dedicated pool for a benchmark, what size GPU should we test? 1x A100 or multi-gpu?
06:46 Jared: start with 1x A100/80GB equivalent or an H100 if available. For batch workloads we recommend a 2-GPU pool for predictable throughput. We'll send recommended cluster configs.

07:12 Priya: small note on auth — we want SSO and KMS integration for keys, is that covered in Private deployment or also for Dedicated?
07:21 Maya: Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS via a key delegation pattern; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full KMS/HSM integration. For SSO we have SAML and OIDC for the console; API keys can be rotated and tied to service accounts.
07:33 Priya: great, and audit logs for inference calls? we need token-level retention for 90 days.
07:39 Maya: audit logs are available, we can configure retention and mask sensitive parts. note that hosted mode will have different retention SLAs than Private. for regulatory we typically recommend Private.

08:05 Tom: back to integration — we tried the tool-calling where the tool executed HTTP to our inventory service. in some runs the tool output timing pushed model output later. how do we instrument that?
08:16 Jared: instrument in two places: tool execution time reported back in the model trace, and route-level metrics in the console (per-route latency breakdown: model time, tool time, network). we can surface tool latencies as a separate column.
08:29 Sara: can we get trace IDs in the response to correlate logs?
08:33 Jared: yes we emit a request_id and a trace_id that you can pass into your logging correlation. SDK will also attach span headers.

09:02 Priya: on output validation we saw that the SDK's 'coerce' option changed a numeric sku from "00123" to 123 which broke our downstream joins. is there a way to preserve formatting?
09:13 Jared: yes, avoid 'coerce' or set string-preserve for those fields. the schema supports a pattern: {type: 'string', pattern: '^0[0-9]+'} to keep leading zeros. we'll add an example.

10:00 Maya: quick demo time? jared you wanna show the updated SDK sample and the small local app?
10:05 Jared: sure — (demo noise) so here's the repo https://redwood.example/sdks/atlas-integration with three examples: streaming+tools, strict-structured example, and resume/retry snippet. i'm going to paste the resume snippet in chat — (paste)
10:22 Jared (reads): "await client.generate.resume({requestId})" — client handles merging streamed chunks and validating structured output on finalization.
10:34 Priya: that resume helper would help. when stream cut we can call resume then reassemble — but one question — if resume fails do we get the partial?
10:41 Jared: resume will return either a completed result or an explicit resume-failed error; in the latter case the SDK returns the last successfully validated attempt under 'last_valid'. so you won't drop to an inconsistent state.

12:00 Tom: regarding structured examples, do you support multiple alternative schemas (e.g., product vs offer) in one call? sometimes the model picks variant A or B.
12:09 Jared: you can pass a union schema array and choose an 'expected' field. if multiple match, the SDK returns all matches with scores; we also support a 'prefer_schema' hint to bias generation.

15:30 Sara: performance question — streaming + function-calls seems to increase CPU usage on the edge aggregator; are there recommended batching parameters?
15:40 Jared: yep, use continuous batching with a max_wait of 20ms and a max_batch_size tuned to your latency needs. Redwood's runtime will coalesce requests and still honor p95. we'll provide recommended batch curves based on your traffic pattern.

18:00 Priya: one more bug from last run: when the function returned nested arrays, the structured schema validation failed with a 'maxDepth' runtime error in our validator. is that a known issue?
18:12 Jared: hmm could be your local JSON parser limiting depth. Redwood's validator supports deep nested arrays; if you're piping through a middleware that limits depth, that'll surface. we'll check your sample. also we have a 'flatten' option in the SDK that will normalize nested arrays into tokens but that changes semantics so be careful.

20:00 Maya: ok let's capture explicit next steps — and timeline.
20:06 Tom: i'll annotate product acceptance criteria: 1) structured output always parses to canonical schema for 95% of production events; 2) UI does not crash on truncated responses; 3) p95 latency under 400ms for main route.
20:20 Maya: good, Redwood to supply SDK examples + Dedicated cluster for benchmarks by May 12.
20:28 Priya: Atlas to run 10k events through the Dedicated cluster and share logs by May 14.
20:35 Jared: i'll also add a regression test harness we can run against your sample events; will push to the repo.

Crosstalk/side notes (approx timestamps):

27:30 Priya: please do — we have a cost target of $0.004 per API call on avg.
27:36 Jared: okay we'll produce an estimate.

34:00 Maya: any other blockers?
34:05 Tom: just want clear UX mapping when validation fails — will we get an error code to map?
34:12 Jared: yes error codes with friendly message and a 'validation_hint' blob for UI to show next steps.

41:00 Maya: recap and next steps — Redwood: SDK examples, Dedicated cluster setup and benchmark run, security pack and SOC2 docs. Atlas: sample events, run 10k pipeline, report logs. schedule follow-up benchmark sync for week of 2026-05-18.
41:30 Priya: sounds good.
41:34 Tom: thanks all.
41:36 Maya: thank you — we'll send notes and I'll follow up with repo and creds.
41:45 End of call.
